title: China to Punish Communist Officials Who Support Dalai Lama
main_content:
China is threatening to punish Communist Party members loyal to exiled Tibetan spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, whom Beijing regards as a dangerous separatist.

Ye Dongsong, with the party’s internal discipline watchdog, warned Tibet authorities to focus on “neutralizing separatists and maintaining social stability.”

Ye’s comments were published in the Global Times, which quoted analysts who said, “Some officials in Tibet still sympathize with the Dalai Lama” because of their religious beliefs.

The article provided no estimation of how many Communist Party officials have sympathies or links with the exiled Tibetan spiritual leader.

questions.question: How do Chinese leaders regard the Dalai Lama?
options: As a respected spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism
As a dangerous separatist threatening national unity
As a cultural icon promoting Tibetan heritage
As an irrelevant figure in modern Chinese politics
questions.answer: As a dangerous separatist threatening national unity

questions.question: Why do some officials in Tibet sympathize with the Dalai Lama?
options: Due to political pressure from the international community
Because of their personal connections with him
As a result of their religious beliefs
To gain favor with the local population
questions.answer: As a result of their religious beliefs

questions.question: What did the article say about the number of Communist Party officials who sympathize with or have links to the Dalai Lama?
options: It said the number was very small
It said the number was increasing rapidly
It said the number was already known exactly
